message.content:
Building a new PC can be a rewarding project, and it’s easier than you might think if you follow a clear plan. Below is a step‑by‑step guide that covers everything from choosing parts to putting them together and getting your system up and running.

---

## 1. Plan Your Build

| Decision | Why It Matters | Tips |
|----------|----------------|------|
| **Purpose** (gaming, content creation, office work, etc.) | Determines which components will deliver the best performance for your needs. | List the software or games you’ll run; check their recommended specs. |
| **Budget** | Keeps you from overspending or underspecifying. | Allocate roughly 30–40 % of your budget to the GPU, 20–25 % to CPU, 15–20 % to storage, 10–15 % to motherboard & PSU, rest to peripherals. |
| **Form Factor** (ATX, Micro‑ATX, Mini‑ITX) | Affects case size, cooling options, and future upgradeability. | ATX gives more room for cooling and expansion; Mini‑ITX saves space but limits upgrades. |

### Quick Checklist
- **CPU** – Core i5/i7/i9, Ryzen 5/7/9, or equivalent.
- **GPU** – RTX 3060/3070/3080, Radeon RX 6600/6700/6800, etc.
- **Motherboard** – Compatible socket, chipset, form factor.
- **RAM** – 16 GB DDR4/DDR5 (dual‑channel).
- **Storage** – NVMe SSD (500 GB+) + optional SATA HDD.
- **Power Supply** – 650–850 W, 80+ Gold or better.
- **Case** – Good airflow, cable management, enough space for GPU length.
- **Cooling** – Stock cooler or aftermarket air/liquid cooler.
- **Peripherals** – Monitor, keyboard, mouse, speakers/headset.

---

## 2. Gather Your Parts

| Component | Typical Choices | Notes |
|-----------|-----------------|-------|
| **CPU** | Intel Core i5‑13600K / AMD Ryzen 5 7600X | Overclockable if you’re comfortable. |
| **GPU** | NVIDIA RTX 4070 / AMD Radeon RX 7800 XT | Check VRAM (8 GB+). |
| **Motherboard** | ASUS TUF Gaming Z790 / MSI MPG B650 Tomahawk | Ensure BIOS supports your CPU out‑of‑the‑box. |
| **RAM** | Corsair Vengeance LPX 32 GB DDR5‑5200 | Dual‑channel kit. |
| **SSD** | Samsung 980 PRO 1 TB NVMe | Fast boot and load times. |
| **HDD** | Seagate Barracuda 2 TB 7200 RPM | For bulk storage. |
| **PSU** | EVGA SuperNOVA 750 W 80+ Gold | Modular for clean cables. |
| **Case** | NZXT H510 / Fractal Design Meshify C | Good airflow, cable routing. |
| **Cooler** | Cooler Master Hyper 212 EVO | Air cooler; liquid cooler if overclocking heavily. |

> **Tip:** Use online PC builders like PCPartPicker to avoid compatibility issues and get price comparisons.

---

## 3. Prepare Your Workspace

1. **Clean, flat surface** – Avoid clutter.
2. **Anti‑static wrist strap** – Ground yourself before touching components.
3. **Tools** – Phillips screwdriver, tweezers, cable ties.
4. **Lighting** – Bright LED lamp or flashlight.

---

## 4. Install the CPU

1. Open the CPU socket latch.
2. Align the CPU (gold triangle) with the socket.
3. Gently place the CPU; do not force it.
4. Lock the socket latch back down.

---

## 5. Apply Thermal Paste & Mount Cooler

- If using an aftermarket cooler, apply a pea‑size amount of thermal paste on the CPU center.
- Attach the cooler according to its manual (screw or clip system).
- Connect the fan header to the motherboard.

---

## 6. Insert RAM

1. Open the DIMM slots’ latches.
2. Align the notch on the RAM stick with the slot.
3. Firmly press until the latches click into place.

---

## 7. Mount the Motherboard

1. Place standoffs in the case matching the motherboard holes.
2. Align the motherboard with the I/O shield and standoffs.
3. Secure with screws (do not overtighten).

---

## 8. Install Storage

- **NVMe SSD**: Slide into M.2 slot, screw down.
- **SATA HDD**: Mount in drive bay, connect SATA data & power cables.

---

## 9. Power Supply Installation

1. Slide PSU into the case (bottom or top depending on design).
2. Screw it in securely.
3. Route cables neatly; use cable ties.

---

## 10. Connect Power Cables

| Cable | Connection |
|-------|------------|
| 24‑pin ATX | Motherboard main power |
| 8‑pin EPS | CPU power |
| PCIe 8‑pin/12‑pin | GPU |
| SATA power | HDD/SSD |
| SATA data | HDD/SSD |
| Front panel connectors | USB, audio, power button, reset button |

> **Note:** Refer to the motherboard manual for exact pinouts.

---

## 11. Install the GPU

1. Remove the appropriate rear expansion slot covers.
2. Align the GPU with the PCIe x16 slot.
3. Push firmly until it clicks into place.
4. Secure with screws.
5. Connect required PCIe power cables.

---

## 12. Final Cable Management

- Bundle cables with ties.
- Route cables behind the motherboard tray.
- Keep the front panel cables tidy.

---

## 13. First Boot & BIOS Setup

1. Connect monitor, keyboard, mouse.
2. Power on; enter BIOS (usually `Del` or `F2`).
3. Verify:
   - CPU, RAM, storage detected.
   - XMP profile enabled for RAM.
   - Boot priority set to SSD.
4. Save & exit.

---

## 14. Install Operating System

1. Create a bootable USB with Windows 10/11 or Linux distro.
2. Boot from USB; install OS onto NVMe SSD.
3. Follow on‑screen prompts.

---

## 15. Install Drivers & Software

- **Chipset drivers** – From motherboard manufacturer.
- **GPU drivers** – NVIDIA GeForce Experience or AMD Radeon Software.
- **Other peripherals** – Keyboard, mouse, sound card.
- **Utilities** – HWMonitor, MSI Afterburner, etc.

---

## 16. Test Performance

- Run benchmarks (Cinebench R23, 3DMark, Unigine Heaven).
- Stress test GPU (Unigine Valley, FurMark).
- Monitor temperatures (HWMonitor, GPU-Z).

---

## 17. Troubleshooting Common Issues

| Symptom | Likely Cause | Fix |
|---------|--------------|-----|
| No display | GPU not seated, missing power cable | Re-seat GPU, double‑check power |
| Random reboots | Overheating, insufficient PSU | Clean fans, ensure proper airflow, verify PSU wattage |
| BIOS not detecting GPU | Wrong PCIe slot, missing power | Move GPU to primary slot, confirm power connection |
| Driver errors | Outdated drivers | Update via manufacturer site |

---

## 17. Enjoy Your New PC!

- Set up your favorite games or productivity apps.
- Customize lighting (if supported).
- Keep drivers updated for optimal performance.

---

### Quick Reference Links

- [PCPartPicker](https://pcpartpicker.com/) – Compatibility checker.
- [AnandTech Bench](https://www.anandtech.com/show/bench) – Benchmark results.
- [MSI Afterburner](https://www.msi.com/page/afterburner) – GPU monitoring & overclocking.

Happy building! If you hit a snag or have questions about specific components, feel free to ask.
